notes.title: Animals and other features - Progress update
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

Once again, it's been a while since I checked in with you all. I'm very aware that around now is when I had hoped to have this update finished, but I've been working an actual job, which has relegated Into the Wild's development to something I can only do in my free time. Nonetheless, I have been working away when I can find the time, and whilst sadly I'm not delivering this update to you all today, I can at least talk more about what will be in it and when you can expect it.

So! Animals, the most exciting feature coming to this update and the thing I'm personally most excited about having in the game. Well, the good news is, they're basically done! Coming in this update are 2 animals which will inhabit the valley of Jegersdal, and you've probably already spotted one of them from this update's thumbnail: wolves. Wolves will be a new threat that players have to deal with, as they will roam the valley seeking out food, and given that food is already somewhat rare in the region, that could very well mean you! In real life wolves are very good hunters with keen vision and a strong sense of smell, and the wolves that are coming to Into the Wild are no different, with them being able to detect players from fairly long distances by sight and even by smell alone in situations where visibility is less than ideal. Wolves will stalk you and try and stay out of your line of sight to let them get as close as possible before they begin the charge to try and take you down, and if you let them get close enough then they can do that fairly easily, with wolf attacks often being fatal without means to fight back.

But, it wouldn't be very much fun if you actually couldn't fight back at all! Being added along with the wolves is the ability to finally pick up and use the rifle that already exists in the game, as well as adding ammunition for it in a few places. Players will need to aim carefully, as their character has little to no weapon skills and handles the rifle accordingly, but thankfully the rifle is powerful enough to bring down a wolf in a single hit. Managing to take down a wolf can be quite rewarding, as you can harvest the dead corpse for it's meat to sustain yourself that little bit longer. That being said, if you're really too scared to go up against them, hostile wildlife can be turned off through a toggle when starting a new game, and this can be used to have them either active or inactive on both difficulty settings.

However, not all wildlife coming in this update is hostile, because in addition to wolves, rabbits are also being added to the game! Acting as a source of food for both you and the wolves, you'll often find rabbits wandering the more forested areas of the valley. You'll be able to use the rifle to hunt the rabbits for food to keep yourself going past the point that was possible with just the base game food items, although with their small size and their tendency to run away from the slightest noise or movement, you may find them even harder to hit than the wolves!

So, those are the big features of this update! I am working on some smaller quality of life additions as well. As mentioned in my last post, this update should come with improvements to the fall damage system, as well as some retexturing to make the game look a bit nicer. These improvements are somewhat secondary to getting the wildlife done and added to the game though, and may actually end up arriving either only partially in this update or even get completely pushed back.

Lastly, the big question: when is this update coming? Well, as mentioned, most of the core systems for both the wolves and the addition of the rifle are finished and I'm in the polishing stages for that. There are, of course, some glitches, and I've been really struggling with animations for the rifle (although the animals animations are actually finished), which need to be sorted out prior to release, but this content is definitely on the home stretch now. My plan is to release this update, regardless of how much of the extra stuff is finished, at the start of January 2025. 

This means that the animals and the rifle will, unless some unforeseen disaster takes place, definitely be coming on that date. What remains up in the air is how much of the other stuff get's thrown in there and how much is delayed for a later date. The optional stuff is: full and complete animations for the rifle, the retexturing, and the fall damage overhaul. If the fall damage isn't in there, then that will be top priority for me, then after that the retexturing, and finally an update that will add not only animations to the rifle but to the other items as well. But for now, I'm going to focus on getting everything that I can shipped with this update and then look at a plan for the other content afterwards.

I'm really excited to deliver this all to you at the start of the new year!

Seph

notes.title: The future of Into the Wild
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

So, it's been a while since I checked in with you all! Honestly, burn out hit me like a truck after Into the Wild released, it was a VERY tiring year working on getting this game out to you all, so I needed to step away for a bit. That being said, seeing everyone playing Into the Wild over the last nearly 2 months has been a dream come true for me and I absolutely plan to continue working on Into the Wild.

As I mentioned in a previous announcement a while back, because of me using Into the Wild as my masters project, I wasn't able to patch the game while my submission was still being graded. Well, that grading period is over and I can start to look at getting new content pushed out to you all! I've been looking at the feedback that Into the Wild has received, both good and bad, and thinking about where to go from here. I'm really glad that so many people played Into the Wild and found something in it that they enjoyed, and I'm also aware that the game has a lot of flaws that hindered peoples game experiences.

As such, for the last couple of weeks I've been working on a fairly large update that should bring some cool new features to the game, as well as fix some of the existing problems. Progress is actually fairly far along with this update, as I've had time to work on some of the new features in the time that I couldn't patch the game, I just didn't want to announce it to you all until I knew that I was in the clear to start releasing new content.

So! Into the Wild's version 1.1.0 update should add into the game:
[list]
[*] Wildlife! Both passive wildlife that can be hunted for food, like rabbits, and hostile wildlife that will actively attempt to attack you, like wolves
[*] New items! Most significantly firearms and ammunition for either hunting or self-defense to go along with the addition of wildlife, but a few smaller additions as well
[*] Updated environment! A lot of improvements to the existing game environment to add more detail and to (hopefully) fix the pretty abysmal texture tiling that is currently in the game
[*] Overhauled fall damage! This system really kinda sucked to a degree that I hadn't realized prior to the games release, so I've been working on completely ripping out the old system and making a new one from scratch 
[/list]

I don't have an exact ETA for this update just yet. The wildlife and firearms are both very close to finished, I'm mainly just struggling with animations since animating really isn't my strong point. I hope that this update will get pushed out sometime in late October to early November, but I really can't say for sure, and I'll update you guys with more specifics about the content in the update as well as a more accurate time you can expect it as we get closer to it's completion.

Once this update comes out, I can say with at least some degree of confidence that I will be continuing to work on new content, as I have a lot of ideas for where to take the game and what to improve in it. But, I want to stay grounded in the present, so we can look at what comes after this update once I've got these features pushed out to you.

I'm really excited for you guys to try the improved Into the Wild in another month or so!

Seph

notes.title: Version 1.0.4
notes.content:
Hello all!

Been a little bit since the last update, but got some new bug fixes! The new fixes are: 
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where hunger, health and cold could still deplete while intro screen was showing
[*] Fixed a bug that caused music to overlap in certain situations
[*] Fixed a problem where standing on top of certain objects would cause the player to instantly die. Unfortunately a fix for this happening at all requires a fall damage overhaul, but as a stop gap measure I have prevented it from happening in the most prevalent locations
[*] Fixed a bug with the music system that caused certain tracks to play in very unfitting situations
[*] Fixed a bug that was causing stamina to not regenerate at the correct speed
[*] Fixed a bug in one of the caves that was frequently causing players to fall through the map
[/list]
The next thing on my list is to overhaul the fall damage system, although I'll keep up with minor patches like this. This has been a problem since day 1 of Into the Wild, and is probably the largest thing holding the game back at the moment. What I'm planning to do is to completely rip out the old fall damage system and build a new one from scratch, so expect it to take a while, but know that I am working on it!

Seph

notes.title: Version 1.0.2
notes.content:
Hello all!

This is quite a boring patch, nothing really exciting happening apart from fixing some notable bugs. The changes are:
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug that caused players to be able to eat the same food item multiple times
[*] Improved snow collisions to make it come into buildings and caves less
[*] Adjusted the algorithm that plays voice lines so that the game doesn't always decide to play hunger related lines even when a player is freezing or close to death
[*] Fixed a bug that caused the game to only play hunger lines for the first level of hunger rather than progress through the different voice lines as a player gets more hungry
[*] Fixed a bug that caused health to not deplete properly under some circumstances
[*] Fixed a bug that prevented background audio from being made quieter when certain voice lines played
[*] Fixed a bug that caused music to play quieter than it should
[*] Fixed a bug that allowed players to move during sleep
[/list]
It's been amazing seeing the support for Into the Wild the last few days, thank you so much to each and every one of you who has played the game. There's been a lot of feedback thrown my way, both positive and negative, and I've been thinking on all of it and considering the direction I want to take with Into the Wild, but for now let's just enjoy release week and I'll throw up a post soon about what's coming next

Seph

notes.title: Version 0.3.4 - Hotfix 1
notes.content:
Hello again everyone!

I don't usually tend to make announcements for these kind of small updates where it's mostly fixing bugs and not much new content, but todays fix comes with some fairly significant changes I wanted to let you all know about!

So, the weather system. It's been a frustrating part of the game for a while now, as it has been widely considered too harsh and not changeable enough. Well, no longer! Along with a variety of bug fixes, this update brings out a rather substantial overhaul to how the game decides which weather it is going to change to as well as how frequently the weather changes.

The new weather system has 3 key changes. The first of these is that there will now be a longer amount of time between weather changes. According to my maths, the weather should (on average) take around 1.5 times as long to change as it did previously. Of course, it's still subject to randomness, but the probability of it changing within 6 hours of the last change has been significantly lowered. Whilst this change might seem counter-intuitive with what I'm trying to achieve with this update, it makes sense to balance out the second change to the weather system.

This second change is that the weather system is now MUCH more sensitive to the weather staying either good or bad, and will adjust accordingly. It's now significantly less likely to have either bad or good weather for more than 3-4 changes of the weather. In practicality, this means that it's very unlikely for the weather to stay either good or bad for more than 2 in game days. This is why the time it takes between weather changes had to be increased, as with only the overhaul to the system that picks the new weather type it would frequently change from completely clear weather to a blizzard in the space of less than 24 in game hours.

The final change is that the weather can jump larger distances in qualities of weather. What this means, to use an example, is that previously it was only possible for the weather to go from a blizzard to heavy snow, to light snow, to cloud and finally to clear. With the new system it could go from blizzard to light snow and then to clear, skipping out several steps in the process and making changes from bad to good weather and vice versa take less time. If the weather has been of neutral quality these larger jumps aren't particularly likely, but if the game detects that the weather has been either good or bad for a long period they become more and more likely. 

These changes are still quite experimental, but based on my own testing, it seems like this should go at least some way to alleviating the problems with the weather system. Of course, this is based on my own thoughts as a dev, which is why I want to push this new system out to you, the players. If this weather system doesn't work out, then I will of course revert back to how it was previously in either the next update or another hotfix. Alternatively, potentially this update doesn't go far enough to fixing the problems with the weather system, in which case I'll look at how the same changes can be continued so the weather system stays moving in the right direction. Or maybe even this time I got it just right... only time will tell!

Anyways, enough talk about technicalities, I hope you enjoy the changes to the weather system and the bug fixes along with this update, and make sure to let me know what you think!

Seph
